title: Lower one input
prompt:
Choose one thing to soften: sound, light,
temperature, or texture. Change just that thing
and notice whether your body gets a little more
room.
reflection:
What signal is my body giving me before words
arrive?
small: Move a little farther from the input.

title: Find a steady point
prompt:
Notice your feet on the floor, your back
against a chair, or an object in your hand.
Stay with the sensation for three breaths, or
simply name it.
reflection: Which anchor feels most like mine today?
small: Notice the anchor once.

title: Take a sensory pause
prompt:
Step away from the busiest input for a few
minutes. Choose a quieter spot and let your
eyes rest on something uncomplicated.
reflection:
What input would I choose to step away from
first?
small: Turn away from a screen for a moment.

title: Check what your senses need
prompt:
Ask: is there too much input, too little, or
one uncomfortable sensation? Choose one small
adjustment that matches.
reflection:
What does my sensory system seem to be asking
for?
small: Choose less, more, or different.

title: Rest your eyes
prompt:
Let your gaze settle on a calm, still object or
close your eyes if that feels comfortable. Give
your visual system a short break.
reflection: What helps my attention feel less crowded?
small:
Look away from the busiest part of the
room.

title: Choose comfortable pressure
prompt:
If pressure feels good to you, lean into a
cushion or wrap in a familiar blanket. Stop or
change it if it feels uncomfortable.
reflection:
Does pressure feel comforting, neutral, or not
for me?
small: Rest your hands on a pillow.

title: Make sound more predictable
prompt:
Choose a familiar sound or song at a
comfortable volume. Reduce unexpected audio if
you can, and give yourself permission to pause
it.
reflection: Which sounds feel familiar or settling to me?
small: Turn one sound down or off.

title: Adjust temperature
prompt:
Notice whether you feel too warm or too cool.
Change one layer, move to a different spot, or
use a familiar comfort item.
reflection:
What temperature helps me feel more at home in
my body?
small: Loosen or add one clothing layer.

title: Clear one visual patch
prompt:
Choose one small area in your view and make it
simpler: close a tab, move one object, or face
a plain wall.
reflection:
What would make this small visual space feel
more like mine?
small: Turn your chair or body slightly.

title: Find a familiar texture
prompt:
Touch a fabric or object that usually feels
comfortable. Notice its texture without needing
to make the sensation go away.
reflection:
What personal memory or association comes with
this texture?
small: Keep a familiar object nearby.

title: Lower the light
prompt:
If light feels harsh, move away from glare,
close a curtain, or adjust one light source.
Keep enough light to feel safe and comfortable.
reflection: What kind of light supports me best right now?
small: Turn away from the brightest source.

title: Create one quiet zone
prompt:
Choose a small place to pause where fewer
things are happening. It does not need to be
perfectly quiet or tidy.
reflection:
Which places let my nervous system exhale a
little?
small: Stand by a doorway for a minute.

title: Change your posture
prompt:
Try a position that gives your body more
support: feet down, back supported, or a pillow
under an arm.
reflection: What position gives me the support I need?
small: Shift one part of your body.

title: Make a softer transition
prompt:
Before switching tasks, give yourself a short
warning and one simple cue for what comes next.
reflection: What transition cue would respect my pace?
small: Say the next step aloud once.

title: Let your body stim
prompt:
If it feels safe and comfortable, allow a small
repetitive movement or sound that helps you
regulate.
reflection:
Which movements feel regulating or enjoyable to
me?
small: Move one hand or foot freely.

title: Reduce competing sounds
prompt:
Choose the sound that matters most right now.
Pause or lower another source, such as a video,
notification, or background track.
reflection: What sound can I choose to let go of for now?
small: Mute one notification or app.

title: Ask for a sensory change
prompt:
Try a direct request: 'Could we lower the
volume?' or 'Can I sit somewhere quieter?' You
can ask without explaining everything.
reflection:
What request would help me feel safer or more
comfortable?
small: Write the request before saying it.

title: Plan a way to step out
prompt:
If you are entering a busy place, decide where
you can pause and how you can leave if you need
to.
reflection: What clue tells me I may need a break or exit?
small: Identify one nearby quieter spot.

title: Use a sensory boundary
prompt:
Choose one limit for now, such as no extra
audio, fewer questions, or a few minutes
without conversation.
reflection:
Which sensory limit matters most to me in this
moment?
small: Ask for one minute of quiet.

title: Notice one neutral sensation
prompt:
Find something your body can notice without
judging it: feet on the floor, air on your
hands, or a chair supporting you.
reflection: What neutral sensation feels easiest to notice?
small: Name one physical sensation.

title: One basic need
prompt:
Scan for water, food, bathroom, temperature,
medication routine, or rest. Pick the one that
would make the next ten minutes easier.
reflection:
What kind of care fits my life today, rather
than an ideal routine?
small: Bring the needed item closer.

title: Minimum viable wash
prompt:
Choose one care step: rinse your face, brush
briefly, change one clothing item, or use a
wipe. Partial care still counts.
reflection:
Which small act feels respectful of my body
right now?
small: Put the item within reach.

title: Food with fewer steps
prompt:
Choose the easiest available food that feels
manageable. Pairing ready-to-eat things is
enough; this is about some fuel.
reflection:
What food feels familiar and possible, not
perfect?
small: Pick the first familiar option.

title: Rest without earning it
prompt:
Let one demand wait while you sit or lie
somewhere comfortable for a few minutes.
reflection:
Can rest and responsibility both matter without
solving them now?
small: Lean back for one minute.

title: Put water in reach
prompt:
Place a drink where you are likely to see it.
Take a sip when you want; there is no need to
finish it now.
reflection: What cue makes drinking easier for me?
small: Move the glass or bottle closer.

title: Make the bathroom step smaller
prompt:
If you need the bathroom, focus only on getting
to the doorway or standing up. Decide on the
next step after that.
reflection: What is the smallest step my body can agree to?
small: Put both feet on the floor.

title: Support a medication routine
prompt:
If you have prescribed medication, use your
usual instructions. A reminder, visible pack,
or routine cue may make the step easier.
reflection: What routine cue already works for me?
small: Set a reminder for the usual time.

title: Clear one contact surface
prompt:
Make one small spot usable: a corner of the
bed, chair, or desk. Stop when that spot works
for you.
reflection:
Which one spot would make this space more usable
for me?
small: Move one item out of the way.

title: Choose sensory-comfort clothes
prompt:
Pick the cleanest comfortable option available.
Softness, temperature, and ease matter more
than making an outfit perfect.
reflection: What clothing helps me feel at home in myself?
small: Change one uncomfortable item.

title: Name the next visible step
prompt:
For a task that feels huge, identify one action
you can see and do, such as opening the
document or finding the needed item.
reflection:
What part of this task is actually mine to do
first?
small: Look at the task without starting it.

title: Check your energy, not your worth
prompt:
Ask what your energy can support right now:
pause, a tiny step, or a regular task. Let the
answer guide the size of the plan.
reflection: What does my energy ask me to respect today?
small: Choose between rest and one tiny step.

title: Use one dish
prompt:
For a meal or snack, use one plate, bowl, or
cup that makes cleanup simpler. It does not
need to be a full kitchen reset.
reflection: What does enough look like for this meal?
small: Find one clean or usable dish.

title: Try a two-minute reset
prompt:
Set a short timer and do one small thing that
would help your space or body. Stop when the
timer ends if you want.
reflection:
Which small action would bring a little order
without demanding a full reset?
small: Do one action, without a timer.

title: Use a default choice
prompt:
Reduce a decision by choosing a familiar
default for now: same snack, same seat, or same
easy next step.
reflection:
What familiar choice would free up some decision
energy?
small: Choose the option you already know.

title: Ask for practical support
prompt:
If someone safe is available, make one specific
request: bring water, sit with you, or help
locate an item.
reflection:
What kind of help would feel supportive rather
than intrusive?
small: Draft the request in one sentence.

title: Set up a rest spot
prompt:
Make resting easier by moving one comfort item
nearby, such as a pillow, charger, blanket, or
headphones.
reflection:
What object makes rest feel more welcoming to
me?
small: Choose one item to bring over.

title: Open one admin item
prompt:
For a piece of life admin, open the message or
document and find the next action. You can stop
before doing it.
reflection:
What part of this admin task feels most
important to know?
small: Locate the message or document.

title: Restart gently
prompt:
If a routine has slipped, resume with the next
small opportunity. You do not need to make up
for missed days.
reflection:
What would a kind restart look like in my own
rhythm?
small: Choose one cue for the next time.

title: Give your body a gentle option
prompt:
If it feels okay, stretch your hands, roll your
shoulders, or change position. Skip any
movement that feels uncomfortable.
reflection:
Which movement feels like care rather than
correction?
small: Relax your hands or jaw.

title: Leave a cue for later
prompt:
Make a future step easier by leaving one useful
item visible or writing one short reminder for
yourself.
reflection: What can I leave ready for my future self?
small: Write three words as a reminder.

title: Make one sound
prompt:
Open your music setup and make one sound: tap a
pad, play a note, or listen to a loop. You can
stop there.
reflection:
What kind of expression feels like mine, even if
it is unfinished?
small: Sit near the setup for a moment.

title: Setup only
prompt:
Do one preparation step: put headphones by the
device, clear a small spot, or place the
push-up bar where you can see it.
reflection:
What makes beginning feel safe or inviting for
me?
small: Count preparation as the activity.

title: One-track movement
prompt:
Play one track and move comfortably: sway,
stretch, walk, or move your shoulders while
seated.
reflection:
What changes in me when I move with a sound I
like?
small: Listen to one track without moving.

title: Choose a body-sized version
prompt:
Pick a small version that feels okay: one
stretch, one wall push, a walk to the door, or
a few seconds of dancing.
reflection:
What version of movement belongs to my body
today?
small: Imagine the movement instead.

title: Open the project
prompt:
Open the music project you want to return to.
You do not have to edit or finish anything
today.
reflection:
What does my creative self want from this
session, if anything?
small: Open the app, not the project.

title: Loop something you like
prompt:
Play a familiar loop or section that already
feels good. Let listening be enough; no need to
improve it.
reflection:
Which sounds feel like a familiar inner
landscape?
small: Listen to a short section once.

title: Make a tiny variation
prompt:
Change one sound or note in a loop. Keep the
original if you like it; exploration does not
require a finished result.
reflection:
What small change feels curious rather than
corrective?
small: Imagine one possible change.

title: Listen without evaluating
prompt:
Play a track or project and listen for one
thing you enjoy, without scoring the mix or
deciding whether it is finished.
reflection:
What do I notice when I listen without judging
myself?
small: Notice one sound you like.

title: Turn one control
prompt:
Choose one knob or fader and explore a small
movement. You can undo it or leave it
different.
reflection:
What feeling or image comes up as I move this
control?
small: Touch the control without changing it.

title: Save a musical idea
prompt:
Record or write down one small idea: a rhythm,
texture, phrase, or mood. It can stay
unfinished.
reflection: What part of this idea would I like to remember?
small: Name the idea in a few words.

title: Return to a favorite track
prompt:
Play a track that reliably makes you curious or
energized. Let it be a listening break, not a
productivity tool.
reflection: What does this track help me feel or remember?
small: Queue the track for later.

title: Try a short rhythm
prompt:
Tap a simple rhythm on a pad, desk, or your
knees. Follow the pulse that feels comfortable.
reflection:
What rhythm emerges when I stop trying to get it
right?
small: Tap one beat, then pause.

title: Stretch beside the setup
prompt:
While near your music gear, try one comfortable
shoulder, wrist, or back stretch. Stop if it
feels wrong for your body.
reflection: Which movement feels natural, not performed?
small: Unclench your hands once.

title: Try a supported push
prompt:
If it feels safe, try one wall push or a very
small push-up variation that suits your body.
No set or target is required.
reflection: What does strength mean for my body today?
small: Stand near the bar without using it.

title: Walk to a nearby point
prompt:
Walk to a doorway, window, or another nearby
spot and return if you want. This can be the
whole movement session.
reflection:
What movement would feel like a small return to
myself?
small:
Stand up and sit back down, if
comfortable.

title: Build a four-bar sketch
prompt:
Make a tiny four-bar idea from sounds you
already have. It can be a sketch, not a track.
reflection:
Can I hold both the wish to create and the need
to rest?
small: Choose one sound for a future sketch.

title: Set a stopping point
prompt:
Before starting, choose a kind stopping point:
one loop, one song, or five minutes. You can
stop earlier too.
reflection:
What would curiosity choose if there were no
audience?
small: Choose the stopping point only.

title: Make a no-goal session
prompt:
Spend a few minutes following curiosity: press
a sound, browse a preset, or move to the
rhythm. There is no output target.
reflection:
What stopping point would honor both interest
and capacity?
small: Open one sound and listen.

title: Save before you leave
prompt:
If you made something, save the project or note
one way to find it again. Then you are free to
stop.
reflection:
Which part of me wants play, and which part
wants structure?
small: Write the project name down.

title: Count showing up
prompt:
Acknowledge the contact you made with music or
movement, even if it was just opening the setup
or listening.
reflection:
What is worth appreciating about showing up at
all?
small: Say: I made a small start.

title: Name the state, not a verdict
prompt:
Try a neutral label: 'I feel overloaded' or 'I
am replaying that moment.' A feeling describes
this moment, not all of you.
reflection: What feeling might be present beside this label?
small: Use one word for the state.

title: Fact, story, need
prompt:
Separate what you know happened, what your mind
fears it means, and what you need now. Keep the
three parts distinct.
reflection:
Which need or feeling is missing from the story
I am telling myself?
small: Write only what you know for sure.

title: Pause before replying
prompt:
Draft a response privately and wait before
sending. Later, decide whether to reply,
shorten it, or leave it unanswered.
reflection:
What part of me wants to answer, and what part
wants protection?
small: Mute the chat for ten minutes.

title: After the social sting
prompt:
Reduce input and do one familiar soothing thing
before interpreting the interaction. Revisit it
later if you still want to.
reflection:
What might this intensity be asking me to notice
or care for?
small:
Take a sip of water or move somewhere
quieter.

title: Notice the first cue
prompt:
Check for an early sign of overload or hurt,
such as a tight jaw, faster thoughts, or
wanting to disappear. Naming it can guide a
pause.
reflection:
What early cue deserves my attention without
judgment?
small: Notice one body cue.

title: Find a neutral body cue
prompt:
If it feels okay, notice where your body is
supported. You do not have to relax or change
the feeling.
reflection:
What does supported feel like to me, even
briefly?
small: Notice the chair or floor supporting you.

title: Ground with a choice
prompt:
Choose one present-moment anchor: a color, a
sound, a texture, or the feeling of your feet.
Use whichever is least irritating.
reflection:
Which present-moment anchor feels least
demanding?
small: Name one color you can see.

title: Park the looping thought
prompt:
Write the thought in a note so you do not have
to keep holding it in your mind. You can return
to it later or decide not to.
reflection: What would I like to set down until later?
small: Write a title for the thought.

title: Give rumination a container
prompt:
If it helps, set a short time to think or write
about the issue, then choose one action or a
pause when time is up.
reflection:
What kind of boundary would give this thought a
container?
small: Set a reminder to revisit it later.

title: Use a kinder inner sentence
prompt:
Try speaking to yourself as you would to
someone you care about: clear, honest, and
without insults.
reflection: What would patience with myself sound like?
small: Replace one harsh word with a neutral one.

title: Delay the final conclusion
prompt:
When emotions are intense, let the conclusion
wait until you have had a little time, food,
rest, or less input.
reflection: Can the answer wait while I care for my body?
small: Tell yourself: I can decide later.

title: Orient to right now
prompt:
Name where you are and one thing happening in
the present. You do not need to solve the whole
story in this moment.
reflection:
What is here now, separate from the imagined
future?
small: Say the room or place you are in.

title: Make room for uncertainty
prompt:
Try: 'I do not know yet.' Uncertainty can be
uncomfortable without requiring an immediate
answer.
reflection: What can remain unknown for today?
small: Write 'not sure yet' in a note.

title: Add one possible explanation
prompt:
Without forcing positivity, consider one
explanation that is less self-blaming and still
plausible. You can keep both possibilities
open.
reflection:
What other interpretation can coexist with my
first one?
small: Say: there may be another explanation.

title: Move the thought outside your head
prompt:
Draw, type, or voice-note the thought so it is
visible outside your mind. No need to make it
neat.
reflection:
What image or phrase captures this thought for
me?
small: Record a ten-second voice note.

title: Pause the problem-solving
prompt:
Ask whether action is possible right now. If
not, choose a later time or a small comfort
while the problem waits.
reflection: What can I choose not to solve right now?
small: Write one time to revisit it.

title: Ask for clearer information
prompt:
If uncertainty is about another person's
meaning, consider a direct, low-pressure
question when you feel ready.
reflection:
What question would help me meet the real
situation?
small: Draft one clarification question.

title: Check the evidence gently
prompt:
Notice what supports your fear and what you do
not know yet. Avoid forcing yourself to prove
that everything is fine.
reflection: What do I know, and what am I filling in?
small: List one known fact.

title: Ask what would help now
prompt:
Shift from 'What did I do wrong?' to 'What
would support me in this moment?' Choose one
answer if you can.
reflection: What would my kinder inner voice ask for?
small: Name one thing that might help.

title: Rate the intensity
prompt:
Give the feeling a number from zero to ten. Use
the number to choose rest, support, or a small
next step, not to judge yourself.
reflection:
What kind of support fits this level of
intensity?
small: Choose low, medium, or high.

title: Plan a recovery buffer
prompt:
After social time, give yourself a quiet gap
before the next demand. Choose something
familiar with few decisions.
reflection:
What would a recovery space look like in my own
life?
small: Take two quiet minutes before switching.

title: Reduce the social demand
prompt:
If you want connection but have little
capacity, send one sentence, shorten a call, or
continue another day.
reflection:
Which kind of connection matches my capacity
today?
small:
Say: I need a little time; I will get back
to you.

title: Use a clear boundary
prompt:
Try: 'I cannot do that today'; 'I need quiet
now'; or 'Please send the details in a
message.' You do not need a long defense.
reflection: What need is this boundary helping me protect?
small: Draft the sentence without sending it.

title: Let one mask loosen
prompt:
Choose a low-risk comfort: pause before
answering, use a fidget, ask for clearer
wording, or stop forcing eye contact.
reflection:
What is this social role helping me manage, and
is it safe to adjust?
small:
Notice one thing you wish you could do
freely.

title: Choose a low-effort connection
prompt:
Send a song, meme, or short message to someone
who feels relatively safe. Connection can be
small and asynchronous.
reflection:
Which person feels easier to connect with in my
own way?
small: Save something to share later.

title: Choose your reply time
prompt:
You are allowed to respond when you have
capacity. If useful, send a short
acknowledgment and return to the conversation
later.
reflection:
What response timing respects both me and the
relationship?
small:
Decide when you will check the message
again.

title: Prepare an exit phrase
prompt:
Keep a simple phrase ready for leaving or
pausing, such as 'I need a break' or 'I am
heading out now.'
reflection:
What phrase would help me leave without
overexplaining?
small: Choose one phrase in advance.

title: Clarify instead of guessing
prompt:
When it feels safe, ask what someone meant
rather than carrying every possible
interpretation alone.
reflection:
What could I ask instead of carrying a guess
alone?
small: Draft: 'Could you clarify what you meant?'

title: Ask for your preferred format
prompt:
Request a format that is easier to process,
such as written details, one question at a
time, or a little time to think.
reflection:
Which communication form makes my meaning easier
to share?
small: Name one format that helps you.

title: Share your capacity honestly
prompt:
Try a simple status update: 'I want to talk,
but I have low energy today.' You can be honest
without sharing every detail.
reflection: What part of my capacity feels okay to name?
small: Write the message and decide later.

title: Pause the replay
prompt:
After an awkward moment, do something grounding
before reviewing it. You can choose later
whether anything needs repair.
reflection: Can I let the replay wait until I feel steadier?
small: Take a short break from the conversation.

title: Match plans to your capacity
prompt:
Before agreeing, consider travel, noise,
duration, and recovery time. Suggest a smaller
plan if that fits better.
reflection:
What plan fits my actual sensory and recovery
needs?
small: Ask how long the plan will take.

title: Set up one accommodation
prompt:
For a social plan, choose one support in
advance: a quieter seat, headphones for travel,
a clear end time, or a break option.
reflection:
Which accommodation would help me be present as
myself?
small: Decide where you could take a pause.

title: Connect through an interest
prompt:
Share a topic, track, or detail you enjoy with
someone who might appreciate it. You do not
have to make small talk first.
reflection:
What interest feels like a genuine bridge to
another person?
small: Save one thing you enjoy for later.

title: Keep evidence of what works
prompt:
Note a moment when you felt more comfortable
being yourself. It can be small: clearer words,
a pause, or a familiar interest.
reflection: When do I feel more like myself around others?
small: Write down one thing that felt easier.

title: Allow quiet company
prompt:
If you want company without much conversation,
ask someone safe to sit together, share a room,
or do separate activities nearby.
reflection: What kind of company lets quiet be enough?
small:
Imagine who might feel comfortable for
this.

title: Decline a call kindly
prompt:
If a call is too much, suggest text or another
time. Protecting your capacity can help you
stay connected over time.
reflection:
What would protect my capacity and keep a door
open?
small: Let the call ring and decide afterward.

title: Make a small aftercare ritual
prompt:
After an interaction, choose one familiar
transition: change clothes, listen to a song,
wash your hands, or sit quietly.
reflection:
Which transition helps me return to myself after
social time?
small: Choose one calming cue for afterward.

title: Release eye-contact pressure
prompt:
If it helps, look near someone's face, at an
object, or away while listening. You can attend
without forcing eye contact.
reflection: Where can my eyes rest while I stay engaged?
small: Let your gaze rest somewhere comfortable.

title: Keep a boundary without self-judgment
prompt:
Notice that needing a limit does not make you
uncaring. Choose the boundary that protects
your capacity and values.
reflection:
Can I honor a need without turning it into a
flaw?
small: Name one need without explaining it.
